title: Candy Matson
paragraphs: A stylish San Francisco detective series starring Natalie Masters as private investigator Candy Matson, whose cases mix murder and mystery with sharp dialogue and a distinctly independent heroine.

San Francisco-set female private-eye series created and produced/written by Monty/Monte Masters and starring Natalie Masters. Frozen archive contains twelve surviving regular broadcasts plus the 1949 audition and 1952 revival audition. Surviving-recording dates and collector reconstructions conflict substantially, so chronology disputes are retained additively.

GRH documents the program through 1949 EXbrook audition (April 4, 1949 to April 4, 1949) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], NBC-KGO regular run (1949-06 to 1951-05) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], and 1952 revival audition (September 21, 1952 to September 21, 1952) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Monte Masters (writer on 14 recordings, producer on 9 recordings, and director on 4 recordings), [[person|natalie-masters|Natalie Masters]] (performer on 14 recordings), Henry Leff (performer on 13 recordings), Jack Thomas (performer on 13 recordings), Monte Masters (writer (performer on 9 recordings), Bill Brownell (sound-effects artist on 7 recordings), and Dudley Manlove (announcer on 7 recordings).
The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] (broadcast on network).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include female private investigator, police/private-detective collaboration, San Francisco and Bay Area geography, real-location radio storytelling, sustaining regional network drama, and murder and criminal investigation.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Female private-eye radio lead, Candy Matson chronology and title preservation problem, NBC San Francisco Radio City production, and 1952 Candy Matson revival audition.

Programs with especially strong personnel connections in the GRH knowledge graph include [[show|cbs-radio-workshop|CBS Radio Workshop]] (1 shared credited people), [[show|dragnet|Dragnet]] (1 shared credited people), [[show|fibber-mcgee-and-molly|Fibber McGee and Molly]] (2 shared credited people), [[show|fort-laramie|Fort Laramie]] (1 shared credited people), and [[show|frontier-gentleman|Frontier Gentleman]] (1 shared credited people).
